business_scope.primary_industry_name: Retail Sale via Automated Dropshipping Networks

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (continental European commercial law with direct application of EU law)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union (freedom of establishment and free movement of capital)
Belgium-Luxembourg Economic Union (BLEU) bilateral investment treaties in force with third states
Luxembourg double taxation treaties (DTAAs) in force with over 80 jurisdictions
OECD Multilateral Convention to Implement Tax Treaty Related Measures (MLI), as applied by Luxembourg

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended (Articles 710-1 et seq. for SARL); Law of 13 January 2019 establishing the Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE), as amended; Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing, as amended; Law of 19 December 2002 on the Register of Commerce and Companies and Accounting and Annual Accounts of Undertakings, as amended; Regulation (EU) 2015/849 and Regulation (EU) 2018/843 as transposed into Luxembourg law

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarial deed of incorporation and articles of association (acte constitutif / statuts)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarial form filed with the Luxembourg Business Registers; no apostille required for Luxembourg domestic use, but a certified copy bears a Hague Apostille when produced abroad

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of incorporation / recent RCS extract (extrait du registre de commerce et des sociétés)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille via the Luxembourg Ministry of Justice when the extract is used in an Apostille Convention state; otherwise Consular Legalization by a Luxembourg embassy or consulate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good standing and criminal record certificate for each manager/director
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Casier judiciaire du parquet de Luxembourg / Ministry of Justice, Luxembourg
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille if certified for foreign courts or regulators; domestic certification for Luxembourg filings

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Corporate existence and UBO extract for each foreign corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent corporate registry in the country of origin of the shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (Apostille Convention state) or Consular Legalization by the Luxembourg diplomatic mission for non-Convention states

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copy of identification documents (passport) of each shareholder, director, and ultimate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National passport authority or a Luxembourg notary/consular officer certifying the copy
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization for foreign-issued identity documents if not certified by the Luxembourg notary under domestic law

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank certificate of paid-up capital and blocked capital account (attestation de dépôt de fonds)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: No apostille required for Luxembourg domestic incorporation; notarized copy if later submitted abroad

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-incorporation customer due diligence under the amended Law of 12 November 2004; identification and verification of each director, authorized signatory, shareholder and UBO; mandatory screening against the EU consolidated financial sanctions list, the UN Security Council Consolidated List, the OFAC SDN list, and Luxembourg national sanctions registers; Politically Exposed Persons detection and enhanced due diligence where a PEP, family member, or close associate is identified using a documentary source-of-wealth and source-of-funds report; adverse media screening and ongoing monitoring at least semi-annually for this medium-risk automated dropshipping classification.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) / RCS Luxembourg official online portal at www.lbr.lu
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The RCS filing language is predominantly French, with German and Luxembourgish also statutorily recognized; corporate names must be expressed in Latin-script characters; non-Latin names require an approved transliteration into Latin characters; the name must not be misleading, identical to an existing RCS-registered company, or contrary to Luxembourg public order.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Luxembourg does not maintain a formal standalone name reservation mechanism; name availability is assessed by the RCS registrar during document pre-filing. On rejection, the incorporator may within 15 days submit a written re-examination request to the RCS registrar together with amended draft articles. If the registrar maintains the refusal, the applicant may appeal to the Tribunal d'arrondissement de Luxembourg (commercial chamber) within one month of notification under the Luxembourg Code of Civil Procedure. A further appeal lies to the Cour d'appel. Extension of the 30-day clearance window is not generally available; the requester must submit a fresh incorporation application and name clearance request.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A professional domiciliation or administrative agent may be used as the registered office of an SARL, and the RCS accepts a care-of address within Luxembourg. However, a pure virtual office with no local records, no decision-making facility, no local bank account management, and no substantive presence will be insufficient for Luxembourg tax residence and commercial substance purposes. For an automated dropshipping business, a virtual office is permissible at formation stage only if combined with a compliant corporate administration package, actual accounting records kept in Luxembourg, any required VAT registration, and a demonstrable place from which the SARL is managed and controlled.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Estimated 15% annualized probability of an unannounced physical inspection of the registered office for a compliant virtual-office SARL. The probability increases to approximately 30% or higher where the registry or Luxembourg tax authorities identify substance red flags such as repeated address changes, no local bank account, no local accounting records, or inconsistency between the declared activity and the registered office premises.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended (Droit des sociétés), specifically Articles 710-1 through 710-22 governing the Société à Responsabilité Limitée (SARL); Registration governed by the Law of 19 December 2002 on the Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR/RCS).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), operated under the Luxembourg Ministry of Justice.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarial deed of incorporation (acte constitutif) plus electronic application for registration filed through the RCS/LBR e-Registration portal.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum capital is EUR 12,000, fully subscribed and fully paid up before registration. The funds must be deposited in a blocked Luxembourg bank account in the name of the company and held until issuance of the RCS registration extract, operating as an escrow / blocked-capital mechanism.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the subscribers hereby adopt the articles of incorporation of the Société à Responsabilité Limitée (SARL); that the registered office is fixed at 1 Rue de la Libération, L-5171 Niederanven, Luxembourg; that the share capital of EUR 12,000, divided into 120 shares of EUR 100 each, is fully subscribed and allotted to the subscribers as set out in Schedule A; that the shares are accepted and fully paid up; that [Name] is appointed as sole manager, with full power of representation and management; and that the manager is authorised to complete all RCS filings, bank account openings, tax registrations, and administrative formalities required for the company to begin legal operations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pre-incorporation name verification and draft deed preparation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS) and the appointed Luxembourg civil-law notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name availability inquiry through the RCS online portal or instruct the notary to verify the proposed corporate name against the RCS register. Prepare the draft articles of incorporation in French or Luxembourgish covering corporate name, registered office, corporate purpose, share capital, and management powers.
required_dossiers: Proposed name and name verification request
Proof of address for registered office (lease or title deed)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is unavailable or the draft deed is queried, the notary will promptly draft an amended name or deed and resubmit via the same portal; no adverse record attached.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Capital deposit and blocked bank account confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg credit institution or foreign bank branch authorised to provide depositary services for Luxembourg companies
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a blocked capital account in the name of the SARL, deposit the EUR 12,000 minimum capital, and obtain a bank blocking certificate confirming full payment of subscribed capital. The certificate must be issued no earlier than the date of the notarisation and held for release after RCS registration.
required_dossiers: Passport or ID of the sole manager
Proof of physical or professional address
Bank account opening application and mandates
Funds transfer reference proving EUR 12,000 deposit
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank refuses opening due to KYC/AML questions, submit corrected ownership or source-of-funds documentation or instruct another Luxembourg credit institution; the notary can coordinate re-deposit.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg civil-law notary (Chambre des Notaires), competent notary office chosen by the founders
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Execute the authentic incorporation deed before the notary. The notary verifies the legality of the corporate object, capital block certificate, subscribers' capacity, and manager consent, then annexes the instruments and issues the notarial deed.
required_dossiers: Passport/ID, address proof and tax identification of subscribers
Lease agreement or proof of registered office availability
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary flags a defect, the parties execute an amending deed before registration; if the bank certificate expires, a new certificate is obtained and re-deposited.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic filing with the RCS (statutory registration)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – RCS electronic filing department (e-Registration)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the authenticated notarial deed, the capital block certificate, and the registration request through the RCS e-Formalities portal. Pay any applicable court/registry fee. The RCS will assign a registration number and produce the request for entry in the register.
required_dossiers: Identity documents of managers and beneficial owners
Manager's consent to act and specimen signature
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS issues an observation or query, respond within the statutory deadline with a corrected filing or explanatory memo; the notary rectifies minor inconsistencies and resubmits the electronic application.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication in the RESA and issuance of legal-effect registration extract
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: RCS – Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After RCS entry, file the standard legal notice for publication in the RESA (Luxembourg Electronic Collection of Companies and Associations). Obtain the certified RCS extract (extrait) confirming incorporation and legal personality.
required_dossiers: Excerpt of the notarial deed for RESA publication
Names and signatures of managers for RESA notice
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If RESA publication is delayed or contains a typography issue, submit a rectification request to the RCS; publication is retroactive where the statutory formalities are substantially complied with.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax, social security, and administrative registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration des Contributions Directes (ACD), Administration de l'Enregistrement et des Domaines (AED), Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the company's tax registration for corporate income tax and municipal business tax; obtain a VAT number through the AED; register with the CCSS for employer social security if employees are engaged. Provide electronic-commerce activity information to confirm no separate industrial operating licence applies to pure automated dropshipping.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the AED/ACD asks for additional evidence of activity, provide the platform/dropshipping contracts and a brief activity description; any tax or social security registration may be resubmitted online without penalty before first taxable event.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of the Economy – General Directorate for Industry (Direction de l'Industrie); not applicable for pure automated dropshipping / distance-selling activities with no physical production or warehousing in Luxembourg.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: None required – the activity falls under Article 1(1) of the Grand-Ducal Regulation on the free provision of services and does not constitute a classed establishment; no manufacturing permit or operating licence is triggered.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'Environnement (Luxembourg Environmental Protection Agency)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – Category 0 administrative/service activity; no EIA report or registration required because the automated dropshipping model does not involve industrial installations, manufacturing, or chemical storage.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater, VOC, or atmospheric emissions thresholds apply. The activity is governed by general municipal waste-disposal regulations and the obligation to ensure proper disposal of electronic/household waste generated by the office; no environmental standards applicable to the drop-shipped goods because they are shipped directly by suppliers to end customers outside Luxembourg.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety and structural certifications are not required for a non-classed administrative office. The registered office must comply with standard building fire-safety occupancy rules under municipal zoning, and the manager must ensure basic occupational health and safety (ITM inspection standards), including first aid, electrical safety, and exit signage, if employees are engaged in this administrative site.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) / Luxembourg Inland Revenue; registration portal: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) and MyGuichet.lu (for VAT: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT))
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign entities must appoint a Luxembourg tax representative when lacking a permanent establishment, file an application with the AEDT (VAT registration form 640) via MyGuichet.lu, submit certified articles of association, proof of effective management and commercial registration excerpt from the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS), and obtain a Luxembourg VAT identification number (numéro d'identification à la TVA) and national business number (numéro d'identification national) issued by the ACD through the RCS process.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Check-the-box not applicable in Luxembourg; Luxembourg SARL is a taxable entity subject to corporate income tax (impôt sur le revenu des collectivités), municipal business tax (impôt commercial communal), and net wealth tax (impôt sur la fortune). Available elections include: group VAT registration (assujetti unique) under Article 60 of the Luxembourg VAT Law, and the option for a transparent tax treatment of qualifying limited partnerships (not applicable to SARL). Hybrid mismatch rules under ATAD (EU Directive 2016/1164 as transposed) are applied, but no elective hybrid conversion exists for a SARL.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée, TVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 35,000 (annual turnover from taxable supplies of goods or services, excluding VAT, for small enterprise exemption; however mandatory VAT registration applies immediately upon commencement of economic activity with no minimum turnover threshold for cross-border/dropshipping supplies, except the EUR 10,000 distance-selling threshold for intra-EU B2C supplies)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance or digital stamping mandate for domestic B2B invoices. EU e-invoicing directive (2014/55/EU) applies only to public procurement. B2B e-invoicing in a structured electronic format is permitted, subject to authenticity of origin and integrity of content. VAT reporting is periodic (monthly/quarterly) via e-file (eCDF), with SAF-T (Standard Audit File for Tax) required for taxpayers using certified accounting software. No continuous transaction control (CTC) or government clearance escenario.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies to exports of goods to non-EU countries and to supplies dispatched or transported to another EU Member State (intra-Community supply) provided the purchaser is a VAT-registered taxable person. Dropshipping qualifies where the seller (LU SARL) causes the goods to be dispatched to the customer; documentation must prove the physical movement of goods out of Luxembourg or the EU. Offshore services (e.g., digital services to non-EU businesses) qualify under the place-of-supply B2B rule (Article 44 EU VAT Directive) and must not be taxable in Luxembourg.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Administrative Single Document – ASD/DAU) or electronic export declaration (ECS) with MRN (Movement Reference Number)
Bill of Lading (sea) or Air Waybill (air) or CMR (road) evidencing physical dispatch from Luxembourg
Commercial invoice showing the foreign customer and Incoterms (EXW/FCA/CPT/CIP)
Inward Remittance Certificate (proof of receipt of foreign currency payment) or bank statement evidencing settlement
Proof of transport instruction (logistics contract, carrier consignment note, delivery confirmation signed by the foreign customer)
VAT return (VAT declaration) and recapitulative statement (EC Sales List) for intra-Community supplies
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The Luxembourg tax administration (AEDT) may apply anti-abuse measures and impose penalties of EUR 250 to EUR 250,000 or 100% of evaded tax for fraudulent zero-rating claims. Retrospective clawback of VAT, interest at the statutory rate, and criminal fines for customs fraud under the Union Customs Code (UCC) apply. Penalties range from 10% to 200% of deficient VAT based on the degree of intent; criminal sanctions for customs and VAT evasion include imprisonment and seizure of goods. Documentary retention period is 10 years. Missing or false evidence triggers reassessment and denial of zero-rating.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL) and the Luxembourg Financial Sector Supervisory Commission (Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier, CSSF); exchange control enforcement is shared with the Ministère des Finances and the CSSF for financial institutions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg, as a member of the euro area, maintains full capital and current account convertibility for EUR and all foreign currencies. No Luxembourg-specific exchange control legislation restricts cross-border transfers of funds for licensed business entities. Profit remittances, dividends, and repatriated capital are freely transferable, subject only to standard tax withholding compliance (e.g., EU Savings Directive reporting, beneficial ownership declarations) and Anti-Money Laundering (AML) verification requirements. There are no administrative approval hurdles for ordinary commercial payments, loan repayments, or equity injections. For third-country (non-EU) transactions, EU sanctions screening and financial restrictive measures apply, but these do not represent convertibility restrictions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is no statutory surrender or mandatory conversion timeline for export proceeds in Luxembourg. Businesses may retain receipts in any foreign currency, and there is no requirement to convert or repatriate export earnings within a specific period. However, for statistical and balance-of-payments reporting purposes, residents must report cross-border transactions and positions to the BCL through the direct reporting channel (Collecte d'informations Monétaires et Financières, CIMF) if thresholds are exceeded. Export of goods under an automated dropshipping model is classified under ISIC 4791 and is subject to Intrastat and EU customs declarations, but not to FX surrender rules.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (BCEE)

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account / Cross-Border Clearing Hub for EUR-RMB routes

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium legal viability with operational caveats. Electronic Money Institutions (EMIs) licensed in the EEA (e.g., PPS, MANGOPAY, Payoneer, and Luxembourg-licensed EMIs) can hold client funds and provide payment accounts but do not constitute 'credit institutions' for commercial lending or escrow-deposit purposes. For an automated dropshipping entity, an EMI that offers merchant acquiring and mass-payout rails (e.g., Stripe, PayPal) is operationally viable as a payment gateway, but the primary treasury bank account must remain at a fully licensed credit institution to satisfy Luxembourg corporate substance expectations and CSSF oversight. Offshore digital EMIs without a Luxembourg or EEA licence are not legally viable as principal treasury accounts due to proportionality requirements under Luxembourg Circular CSSF 12/552 and the Law of 10 November 2009 on payment services.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote onboarding is permissible in Luxembourg under CSSF AML requirements if the bank applies a risk-based approach and uses certified digital identification (e.g., LuxTrust electronic signature, video identification compliant with EIOPA/AMLD5). However, in practice, domestic Tier-1 banks require at least one director or the ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) to appear in person at the bank's Luxembourg office for the initial interview and to verify the commercial substance of a cross-border dropshipping operation. A fully remote account opening is possible only through certain fintech-friendly banks or EMIs, but for a SARL with non-resident directors and a capital escrow requirement, physical presence of one local representative (often the statutory manager or an appointed bank mandate holder) is strongly recommended to ensure High onboarding viability.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk jurisdiction exposure for non-resident UBO or beneficiary from a non-EU/EEA country without equivalent AML standards
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized and apostilled passport copy, proof of residence, recent regulatory and tax residence certificates, detailed source-of-funds dossier (bank statements, tax returns, audited financial statements of UBO's prior entities), and a written commercial rationale for the Luxembourg wrapper.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Automated dropshipping model flagged as 'transaction-velocity anomaly' with high gross volume and low per-unit margin
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed supplier contracts with freight forwarders and e-commerce platforms (if any), historical transaction logs from Stripe/PayPal, refund/dispute statistics, inventory drop-ship flow diagrams, and a certified independent audit report confirming the absence of unlicensed payment-aggregation activity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Capital escrow contribution from a non-EU parent or third-party lender with unusual tenor or repayment structure
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed loan/subscription agreements, board resolution authorizing the capital injection, evidence of disbursement via transparent banking channel (SWIFT), equivalent AML/KYC documentation for the lender, and a certified copy of the Luxembourg notary deed evidencing share capital formation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: No clear physical operational substance in Luxembourg (virtual mailbox only) and no local tax advisor/appointed director
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Rental agreement for physical registered office, local bank confirmation of active account, employment contracts or service agreements with a local administrative agent, corporate VAT number, and registration at the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS) with a designated local manager.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Electronic payment processor (Stripe/PayPal) held in the name of a foreign entity rather than the Luxembourg SARL
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Updated merchant agreements re-issued to the Luxembourg entity, passport of the entity's UBO and statutory manager, proof of the commercial flows passing through the Luxembourg treasury account, and an AML compliance opinion from a licensed Luxembourg fiduciary.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital contributions must be routed via authenticated SWIFT MT103/MT202 messages from the investor's bank to the Luxembourg SARL's commercial bank account. The purpose code must use the most appropriate EU balance-of-payments (BoP) category: for equity capital, use 'Direct investment – capital' (BoP code 5101) or the corresponding bank-specific code for share capital; for intercompany loans, use 'Loans / Trade credit – other sectors' (BoP code 5103) if applicable. The bank will verify the counterparty's legal existence, the corporate resolution, and the notarized escrow evidence before crediting the Capital Escrow Account. No prior BCL approval is required for such injections, but the BCL may collect statistical details via the reporting entity. Inbound funds from high-risk third countries require enhanced beneficial ownership identification and may trigger extended verification time.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For trade settlements (supplier payments to China, USA, or EU warehouses), the clearing rail should be either (i) a standard international wire via SWIFT MT103 with unambiguous purpose code (e.g., 'Trade Settlement – Goods' under EU BoP 5010), or (ii) a Commercial Letter of Credit (LC) confirmed by a Luxembourg bank when the supplier demands documentary security. For smaller payments within the SEPA zone, a SEPA Credit Transfer (SCT) is acceptable under a Luxembourg IBAN. The payment routing must ensure that the beneficial owner name of the receiving account matches the trade counterparty; otherwise, the Luxembourg bank may reject the payment due to AML sanctions screening. For automated mass payouts to numerous drop-shipping suppliers, an API-based multi-currency payout platform (e.g., via an EMI with an FX licence) is operationally compatible, but every underlying settlement must preserve a traceable audit trail mapped to the Luxembourg treasury ledger.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright FX Forwards (deliverable) for EUR/USD, EUR/CNY, and other fully convertible currencies with a licensed Luxembourg credit institution or an EEA-authorised investment firm
Cross-Currency Swaps (CCS) where the notional exchanges are aligned with the underlying trade payment schedule under an ISDA Master Agreement with a CSA

Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) on restricted currencies (e.g., INR, KRW, VND) only when executed with an authorised counterparty and if the underlying exposure is clearly documented; NDFs are legally permissible but are subject to EU EMIR reporting and mandatory clearing thresholds
FX Options (vanilla and collars) for hedging forecast purchasing exposure, provided the entity has a documented risk-management policy
Overnight EUR/USD swaps only through the central clearing counterparty (CCP) if the counterparty is subject to EMIR clearing obligations

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts (financial statements) filing with the Luxembourg Business Registers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Register of Commerce and Companies (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 7 months after the financial year-end; for a calendar-year SARL, by 31 July of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Directors and managers are subject to criminal fines up to EUR 25,000; the public prosecutor may obtain a court order imposing an astreinte for continuing default; repeated non-filing can trigger compulsory dissolution and strike-off by the RCS.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of beneficial owners (UBO) declaration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Beneficial Owners Register (RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Each calendar year from 1 January to 31 January (annual confirmation window)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file within the January window triggers administrative fines up to EUR 25,000; knowingly providing false or incomplete information may result in criminal penalties.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Luxembourg corporate income tax return (combining corporate income tax, municipal business tax, and net wealth tax)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due no later than 31 December of the year following the tax period; e.g., for a financial year ending 31 December 2024, the return is due by 31 December 2025
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers a surcharge up to 10% of the assessed tax plus late payment interest of 0.8% per month; persistent non-filing may lead to tax-reassessment penalties and criminal sanctions up to EUR 25,000.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A SARL must appoint a statutory auditor (réviseur d'entreprises agréé) if it exceeds at least two of the three medium-size thresholds for two consecutive financial years: balance-sheet total EUR 4.4 million, net turnover EUR 8.8 million, average workforce 50. Regulated entities (credit institutions, insurance, etc.) are always subject to audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP under the law of 19 December 2002 as amended, transposing EU Accounting Directive 2013/34/EU; for consolidated accounts and certain voluntary cases, IFRS as adopted by the EU is permitted.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Any change in beneficial ownership (share transfers, change of percentage interest, change of controlling persons) must be filed with the RBE within one month of the event; in addition, an annual confirmation must be lodged in January each year, even if no changes occurred. The confirmation must be aligned with the last filed UBO particulars and the share register.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: $6,000 – $15,000 (audit fee for a small/medium SARL subject to mandatory statutory audit)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% aggregate headline rate for a Luxembourg City-resident SARL for tax year 2024: 17.00% corporate income tax on taxable income above EUR 175,000, plus 7% solidarity surcharge on the CIT equal to 0.84%, plus municipal business tax of 6.75% applied to the municipal tax base.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Reduced progressive bracket of 15% CIT plus 7% solidarity surcharge and municipal business tax, producing an aggregate effective rate of approximately 22.80% on the first EUR 175,000 of taxable income; 100% participation exemption for qualifying dividends and capital gains (generally 10% minimum shareholding or EUR 6,000,000 acquisition cost and 12-month holding period); 80% exemption for qualifying net income from eligible intellectual property under Article 50bis LIR, reducing the effective tax rate on such income to approximately 4.99%; no statutory tax holiday applies specifically to e-commerce or dropshipping activities.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 300 ('Déclaration pour l'impôt sur le revenu des collectivités, l'impôt commercial communal et l'impôt sur la fortune'), filed electronically through the Luxembourg direct tax administration portal (impotsdirects.public.lu / MyGuichet.lu) using Luxtrust, e-ID, or eLux authentication; paper filing is accepted only in limited cases and delays the processing of the assessment.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within six months after the close of the fiscal year, i.e., by 30 June following a 31 December year-end, pursuant to Article 164 LIR; the ACD normally services an automatic extension to 31 July and, upon reasoned request or via a registered tax advisor, a further extension to 31 December of the following calendar year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Identification page: corporate name, legal form (SARL), registered office address in Luxembourg, RCS registration number, Luxembourg income tax file number, municipal tax file number, fiscal year start and end dates, and precise identification of the responsible director and accounting officer.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The resident Luxembourg SARL is the statutory filer. Non-resident shareholders are identified only in the shareholders' annex and do not file Form 300 on behalf of the company; a non-resident cannot sign the declaration unless formally appointed as a Luxembourg-resident tax representative or manager.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting results: full balance sheet and profit-and-loss account lines reconciled to the statutory annual accounts, including closing inventory, trade receivables, cash positions and operating income; for a dropshipping SARL, all gross sales proceeds, settlement charges, COGS and platform fees must be traceable to Stripe and PayPal statements.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: All foreign-currency sales transactions must be converted into EUR at the European Central Bank reference rate prevailing on the transaction date or on the year-end closing rate consistently applied. Cross-border settlement inflows that are commingled with personal accounts of non-resident directors are a fatal examination point.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconciliation and add-backs: disallowed expenses such as 50% of entertainment costs, 50% of certain passenger-car running costs, penalties, non-deductible taxes, excessive management remuneration paid to directors, and hidden dividend distributions; exempt participating revenues are eliminated here and the taxable reserves and profit appropriations are exchanged.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Payments to non-resident related parties, including dropshipping suppliers, marketing agencies, and foreign group service companies, are deductible only if supported by written contracts, actual service delivery evidence, incoming invoices, and transfer pricing documentation at arm's length. Unsubstantiated wire transfers are treated as constructive dividends.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income computation: determination of the net taxable income after the participation exemption, the IP box deduction, the net wealth tax deduction (Articles 24 and 166 LIR), and the deduction of loss carry-forwards pursuant to Article 114 LIR, which are available for 17 years and forfeited if a more than 50% change in ownership occurs simultaneously with a change of business activity.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Treaty-exempt foreign income and foreign losses must be excluded from the Luxembourg taxable base. The SARL must prove the source and economic ownership of each cross-border profit stream; profits artificially routed through non-resident shell intermediary without substance are re-characterized as taxable Luxembourg income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax computation: calculation of the corporate income tax under the progressive tariff, the 7% solidarity surcharge, the municipal business tax using the municipal coefficient of the commune of the registered office, the application of investment tax credits, and the statement of the net wealth tax base with the allocation of the EUR 500,000 minimum allowance and the minimum tax where applicable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign tax credits are available only under an applicable double tax treaty and are computed line-by-line in the Form 300; non-resident shareholders are not entitled to Luxembourg investment tax credits. The municipal business tax coefficient is fixed by the commune and must match the registered office address.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing exposes the SARL to a 'taxation d'office' by the Luxembourg direct tax administration, a late-filing increase of up to 10% of the assessed corporate income tax under Article 181 LIR, late-payment interest accruing at 0.6% per month (7.2% annualized), administrative fines under Articles 174-177 LIR ranging between EUR 500 and EUR 12,500, and, where concealment is intentional, the criminal anti-evasion surcharge of 10% to 90% of the evaded tax with fines up to EUR 50,000 and imprisonment up to 5 years for the responsible manager.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% domestic Luxembourg withholding tax on dividend distributions made by a Luxembourg SARL to shareholders, applicable to non-resident shareholders and non-resident companies; reduced to 0% for a qualifying EU/EEA parent company holding directly at least 10% of the SARL's capital for at least 12 months under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive, and reduced to 5% or 0% under applicable double tax treaties, commonly 5% for a 10%+ direct shareholding and 0% for EU treaty partners subject to the anti-abuse and beneficial-ownership tests.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke DTA or Parent-Subsidiary Directive relief, the non-resident shareholder must (i) hold the shares in its own name as the ultimate beneficial owner, (ii) obtain a valid Tax Resident Certificate (TRC) from its residence state's competent authority, (iii) complete Luxembourg Form 166 or the applicable certificate-of-residence form, (iv) deliver the certificate to the Luxembourg SARL before the dividend payment date, (v) retain evidence of the minimum shareholding percentage and 12-month holding period, and (vi) ensure the SARL records the reduced-rate distribution in its Form 300 and withholding tax reconciliation; the paying SARL must apply the reduced rate ex ante and, if excess tax has been withheld, the non-resident must apply to the ACD for refund within the statutory limitation period.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Domestic Luxembourg law imposes no withholding tax on ordinary outgoing royalty payments and no withholding tax on conventional interest paid to non-resident recipients (0%); interest or payments on profit-sharing or participating bonds are re-characterised as dividends and subject to the 15% statutory withholding; treaty rates protect the foreign recipient, generally 0% for royalties and 0% to 10% for interest under most Luxembourg DTAs, always conditioned on beneficial ownership, no permanent establishment taint, and economic substance in the recipient jurisdiction.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: No separate statutory Luxembourg local-file threshold exists in the LIR, but a Luxembourg-resident SARL forming part of a multinational group with consolidated annual group revenue of EUR 750,000,000 or more must file or report country-by-country data and would be expected to maintain a Master File and Local File; in operational practice, the Luxembourg direct tax administration requests contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation for all material controlled transactions, and for a dropshipping SARL a Local File is strongly recommended where annual related-party transactions exceed EUR 100,000.
